One entrance.
Two separate albums.

Create the Private Album during setup or add it later. Once created, the matching password opens its album; each album has its own password, encryption keys, and Recovery Code.

Everyday Album

Open with its password, or enable Face ID or Touch ID for quick access, depending on your device.

Private Album

Always requires its own separate password. Media, indexes, and storage are separate from the Everyday Album.

Fold and go.
Open up. See more.

Now on iPhone Duo, folded or unfolded. Photo grids, the viewer, and settings adapt to each screen. iPad also supports portrait and landscape.

Encrypted on device.
Back up where you choose.

No album uploads to the developer

No account, ads, analytics, or tracking SDKs. The developer has no access to album passwords, keys, or Recovery Codes.

Encrypted backup and restore

Choose a destination in Files, with incremental and resumable backups. Restore on another iPhone or iPad using the encrypted backup and matching Recovery Code. Albums do not automatically sync between devices.

Network access

Map network access is on by default and can be turned off in Settings. When enabled, Apple Maps may receive coordinates near where a photo was taken; photo contents are not sent to the map service. System services handle iCloud Photos and your chosen backup location.
